reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Emergent Hartmann procedure in an 82 y in septic shock (norepinephrine 0.12 via peripheral IV, lactate 4.2, AF with RVR) with residual dabigatran (TT over 120, aPTT 54, CrCl 37), idarucizumab available but not given, full stomach, and a family dispute already settled by the HCPOA and ethics.

asa.rationale: Septic shock from perforated viscus on vasopressors with multiple comorbidities; emergency.

decision.rationale: Source control is the treatment. Give idarucizumab before incision, place arterial line before induction, secure central access after reversal, and consent anesthesia with the HCPOA (wife). Ethics found no barrier.

redFlags.evidence: Last dose 2100; TT over 120 s; aPTT 54; CrCl about 37 so prolonged half life.
redFlags.action: Idarucizumab 5 g IV before incision, then central line.

redFlags.evidence: NE 0.12 mcg/kg/min, MAP mid 60s, lactate 4.2, pH 7.28, oliguria 15 mL/h.
redFlags.action: Arterial line before induction, reduced dose induction (etomidate or ketamine), vasopressin and stress dose hydrocortisone if escalating, central line for pressors.

redFlags.finding: Full stomach with vomiting and ileus

redFlags.action: Avoid nodal blockers while on pressors; amiodarone if worsening; treat sepsis.

redFlags.evidence: Son wants DNR and no surgery; wife is designated HCPOA; patient said 'fix it, I want to live'; ethics consulted.
redFlags.action: Anesthesia consent from HCPOA, confirm full code, document.
Redose pip tazo intraop on schedule.

planItems.item: Arterial line before induction; central line after reversal
SICU intubated or extubate if stable
